the generation of spike-and-wave discharges (SWDs) in absence epilepsy, which is the prototype of generalized non-convulsive seizures.

thalamocortex circuits can generate spike and wave discharges at a range of frequencies depending on the type of GABAergic inhibition in the relay cells, and that this mechanism may explain the fast oscillations of absence seizures in the rat.

The main takeaway from our work is that

thalamic relay neurons can be inhibited via two distinct mechanisms: (1) GABAB receptor‐mediated conductances, which are slow, but have a large conductance and (2) GABAA receptor‐mediated synaptic conductances, which have a smaller conductance, but are faster.
